    • Constructor Detail

      • ServiceLoaderSupport

        public ServiceLoaderSupport​(Class<S> serviceInterface)
        Constructor that initializes this instance with the given SPI interface. Every implementation that cannot be loaded counts as unavailable; use ServiceLoaderSupport(Class, Predicate, String) where some failures are an expected property of the classpath rather than a defect.
        Parameters:
        serviceInterface - The interface (or class) for that services should be looked up.

      • ServiceLoaderSupport

        public ServiceLoaderSupport​(Class<S> serviceInterface,
                            Predicate<Throwable> notApplicableClassifier,
                            String notApplicableReason)
        Constructor that also takes the caller's classification of a load failure. An implementation whose failure the classifier accepts is reported as merely not applicable instead of unavailable, so that hasUnavailable() keeps meaning "something is broken". Only the caller knows which failures are expected for its service type, so this class makes no such assumption of its own.
        Parameters:
        serviceInterface - The interface (or class) for that services should be looked up.
        notApplicableClassifier - Decides whether a load failure means the implementation does not fit this classpath rather than being broken. Receives the failure itself, unwrapped from a ServiceConfigurationError but not resolved to its root cause, so it has to walk the cause chain.
        notApplicableReason - Names, for the availability report, why such implementations were skipped.

      • hasUnavailable

        public boolean hasUnavailable()
        Returns whether implementations have been encountered that could not be loaded. Implementations that cannot be loaded are skipped silently, so this only covers the part of the lookup that has been done so far. Implementations the caller's classifier recognized as merely not applicable on this classpath are expected and not counted here.
        Returns:
        true if at least one implementation could not be loaded for any other reason.

      • describeAvailability

        public String describeAvailability​(Function<? super S,​String> nameOf)
        Describes which implementations are available (can be used) and which implementations have been found but could not be loaded, and why. The causes are given by their type and message only, without a stack trace.
        Implementations that cannot be loaded are skipped silently when looking up. This description is intended for being logged when a lookup fails, so that it is visible whether the wanted implementation does not exist, or could not be loaded. Since failing implementations are encountered only when iterating, call this after the lookup that failed. Implementations the caller's classifier recognized as not applicable are listed separately, since that is the only hint about what the classpath is missing when no implementation is available at all.
        Names are listed once each: implementations may share a name, and this description says what is available rather than how many provide it.
        Parameters:
        nameOf - Provides the name of an available implementation.
        Returns:
        A multi-line description.
